h: When Siblings and Parents All Want a Go
p: One of the nicest things about an obstacle course is that it levels the playing field in odd ways. Smaller, lighter kids often zip across hanging sections that bigger adults struggle with, while teenagers bring the power for jumps and climbs. If you've got a family with a wide age range, check how sessions are split by age when you book, so everyone ends up in a slot that suits them.

A good trick for families is to give everyone a different goal. The youngest might aim to finish one section, an older child might try to beat their best time, and a parent might simply aim to get through without needing a sit-down. That way everyone gets a win.

Stoke-on-Trent is full of places to round off the day. The Gladstone Pottery Museum in Longton is a preserved Victorian pottery works, complete with bottle kilns, where you can see how the Potteries made their name. World of Wedgwood at Barlaston lets you explore the famous brand's history and have a go at pottery yourself, and the Emma Bridgewater factory in Hanley is another favourite for a tour and a cuppa.

If you've got animal lovers, Trentham Monkey Forest lets you walk among Barbary macaques in woodland, a real treat for all ages. And Alton Towers is within reach for another day if the thrill-seekers in your family still have energy to spare.
